key_insight: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks can be trained with physics-informed losses to solve free-boundary PDEs by enforcing obstacle, complementarity, PDE, and boundary constraints.
engineering_relevance: This offers a flexible surrogate modeling approach for PDE systems with moving interfaces, such as contact mechanics, phase change, and constrained diffusion.
method: Use KAN function approximators inside a physics-informed framework.
Build the loss from PDE residuals, obstacle inequalities, complementarity terms, and boundary conditions.
Test on linear elliptic obstacle, nonlinear p-Laplacian obstacle, and one-phase Stefan problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports low relative L2 and L∞ errors and accurate recovery of contact regions and moving interfaces, with comparisons against PINN and residual-network baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on carefully balancing multiple residual terms so that inequality and interface constraints are enforced without destabilizing training.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Free-Boundary Partial Differential Equations
